source_text: Ὡσαύτως καὶ αἱ τρεῖς ἡμέραι πρὸ τῶν φωστήρων γεγονυῖαι τύποι εἰσὶν τῆς τριάδος, τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς σοφίας αὐτοῦ. Τετάρτῳ δὲ τύπῳ ἐστὶν ἄνθρωπος ὁ προσδεὴς τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα ᾖ θεός, λόγος, σοφία, ἄνθρωπος.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly also the three days which have come into being before the lights are types of the trinity, of God and of His Word and of His wisdom. On the fourth day, however, the type is the human being who needs light, so that He may be God, Word, Wisdom, human being.

rejected: who is in need of light

correct rendering of the subjunctive mood

pass_b_english: The three days that existed before the lights were created serve as types of the Trinity: God, His Word, and His Wisdom. The fourth day presents humanity as the type that needs light so that God, Word, Wisdom, and human being may all be present.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: Pass B introduces an addition/interpretation not present in the Greek or Pass A: 'so that God, Word, Wisdom, and human being may all be present'. The Greek 'ἵνα ᾖ θεός, λόγος, σοφία, ἄνθρωπος' (so that He may be God, Word, Wisdom, human being) describes the ontological state or identity of the subject, not the 'presence' of the four entities.
reasons: Pass B deviates from the Greek and Pass A by adding 'may all be present' to the final clause, whereas the Greek 'ἵνα ᾖ θεός, λόγος, σοφία, ἄνθρωπος' specifies the identity/being of the subject ('so that He may be...').
